subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm scaling the red panda proportionally to real dimensions—roughly half a meter long with a tail nearly as long—and planning it standing on all fours atop a mossy stone base around 20cm tall.

I'm using a Genshin-style toon kit with cel shading, anime eyes, and fur edges for the visual style, importing the stylized rendering components.

Now I'm working out the skeleton: a hip root, spine chain running from the lower back up to the chest, neck and head joints, a five-segment tail, four legs with IK, and ears, all positioned relative to the stone's top surface height.

For the head I'm placing a scaled skull sphere with a flattened snout, cream cheek ruffs, and large round ears with cream inner rims, then moving on to lay out the body's loft stations connecting hips, spine, and neck with width/height profiles.

The coat uses a fur-edge cel shading scheme: rusty orange over the back fading to dark brown/black on the belly and legs, matching a red panda's coloring. Legs are set up as simple limb chains with bent joints for front elbows and hind knees.

Now I'm shaping the tail as a curved chain of four segments sweeping back and upward from the rump, with radii that taper and widen slightly for a bushy look, then painting it with alternating rust and dark rust rings to get the characteristic ringed tail pattern.

For the face, I'm planning eye decals placed on the skull's surface using an anime-style eye shape with an amber iris.

I'm also working out cream-colored facial markings—cheeks, muzzle, eyebrow spots—and dark tear-streak lines using positional checks relative to the head's center point.

Still working on jaw and ear geometry...

I'm sketching cheek ruffs as small cream spike tufts angled outward, then scattering fur tuft cards across the body surface with tinted grey texture for a furred look. I'm deciding to skip a white chest bib since red pandas have dark chests, and moving on to mottling the stone surface with moss.

For the stone, I'm building a lathe profile with a narrowed rim and flat top, then scattering moss tufts along the upper rim where the surface normal points upward, plus considering whether to add a tiny extra detail like a leaf or glowing sprout, though I'll keep it minimal since it wasn't requested.

Now I'm positioning the stone base so the panda sits balanced on it, placing the tail overhang behind and checking that the front and hind paws land within the stone's radius for visual stability.

Rigging-wise, I'm anchoring the stone to the hips joint since that's the nearest stable root, and mapping out the limb hierarchy—shoulder, elbow, hand bones—so paw spheres sit correctly at each limb tip with small claw spikes added for detail. I'm also setting foot-stone targets at the ground contact points, offset from the root by the leg length.

Now I'm lofting the body shape across several stations relative to the shoulder height, defining width and height at the hips, chest, and shoulders to build the torso silhouette, while keeping the tail chain parented to the hips and figuring out where the chest radius and leg roots should sit along that profile.

Checking leg length against floor clearance so the belly sits just above the ground, then placing the head center and sphere so it overlaps slightly with the body's end station for a seamless neck joint. I'm sizing the eye decals relative to head width and positioning them by azimuth and elevation, then starting on small cream-colored brow spots.

I'm adding a tiny ink-colored nose sphere just below and in front of the head center, and planning a small set of textures for tufts, moss, and eyes. For the paint palette, I'm defining rust, orange, dark, and cream tones along with a darker tail-ring color, and beginning the coat paint setup with a lit edge treatment.

Writing coat shader code...

Adding more spike positioning...

Tail rings will use the sweep chain source for painting. Then I'll move on to the meta export and write everything out.
